title: Optimal Dynamic Subset Sampling: Theory and Applications

problem.claim: Sample a subset of distinct events so that each event is independently included with its associated probability.

gap.claim: Per-event coin flipping takes O(n) time, while an ideal data structure would run proportional to the expected output size, which can be much smaller than n.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies subset sampling for independent events with individual inclusion probabilities.
It contrasts the O(n)-time naive method with a desired output-sensitive method proportional to expected sample size.
Subset sampling is presented as a building block for many tasks and as a research topic spanning more than a decade.

source_observation.claim: The naive approach processes every event, whereas the desired runtime scales with expected output size.

interpretation.claim: When outputs are sparse, output-sensitive data structures may avoid unnecessary work.

application.claim: For sparse independent-selection tasks, evaluate algorithms against expected output size rather than only input size.

exception.claim: The supplied units do not establish that an output-sensitive method exists or is optimal.

unknowns: No proposed algorithm or data-structure design is supplied.
No theoretical guarantees, experiments, numerical results, or application details are supplied.
